# Innovative Solutions For
# **A Sustainable Future**

NMDC Group is an integrated energy and marine services, engineering, procurement, and construction
(EPC) organization with a footprint spanning the MENA region, South Asia, and beyond. We work on
highly ambitious projects, delivering innovative solutions to even the most complex challenges.

[ About Us ][40]

## About NMDC Group

NMDC Group is a prominent figure in the fields of engineering, marine dredging, procurement, and
construction, working in the Middle East and further afield.

We specialize in providing innovative solutions for those vital sectors at the core of the UAE
economy. This includes addressing the complex future challenges facing the energy EPC sector.

Under our umbrella, we own and operate five business units: NMDC Dredging & Marine, NMDC Energy,
NMDC Infra, NMDC Engineering, and NMDC LTS.

[ Read More About NMDC Group ][41]

## Business Units

### NMDC Dredging & Marine

Leading the field of marine dredging, reclamation, and construction, NMDC Dredging & Marine delivers
projects of superior quality. With years of international experience, we are known for our
exceptional track record and commitment to generating true value for all stakeholders.

[ Visit Website ][42]

### NMDC Energy

NMDC Energy is focused on providing engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) solutions to
the energy sector. With comprehensive services tailored to both offshore and onshore clients in the
oil & gas and energy industries, NMDC Energy is designed to continuously meet the industry’s
challenges.

[ Visit Website ][43]

### NMDC Engineering

A leading coastal and marine engineering consultancy, NMDC Engineering has experience working across
marine, civil, hydraulics, geotechnical, and environmental engineering. Across the Arabian Gulf and
the Middle East, NMDC Engineering is enabling the completion of some of the largest marine,
waterfront, and oil & gas infrastructure.

[ Visit Website ][44]

### NMDC Infra

A pioneering construction technology business, NMDC Infra is leading the way when it comes to
precast concrete. With cutting-edge technology and extensive experience, we offer complete,
sustainable, and affordable precast solutions for all construction products, delivering a wide range
of structural and architectural elements.

[ Visit Website ][45]

### NMDC LTS

NMDC LTS (NMDC Logistics & Technical Services) delivers industry-leading support for complex
infrastructure projects, leveraging decades of EPC expertise to ensure seamless execution. With a
solution-driven approach, we drive operational excellence and efficiency across the construction and
industrial sectors, facilitating sustainable growth.

## Norwegian Offshore Wind

Our goal is to establish world leading supply chains within offshore wind. With ~300 members ranging
from agile startups to large offshore wind developers, we are the biggest industry network in
Norway.

We influence policy and political processes on the projects in Norway. We help our members to gain
access and succeed in the key offshore wind markets, especially within floating wind.

## Innovation

Through collaboration, we drive innovation forward to bring costs down.

We aim to build a world leading supply chain within floating offshore wind.

**ORESA - Offshore-Energie nachhaltig denken**

Die Offshore-Erneuerbare-Energien-Branche spielt eine Schlüsselrolle in der Energiewende – doch ihr
Ausbau bringt nicht nur technische, sondern auch ökologische und wirtschaftliche Herausforderungen
mit sich. Das europäische Projekt ORESA (Offshore Renewable Energy Sustainability Alliance) setzt
genau hier an: Es will sicherstellen, dass Nachhaltigkeit nicht als nachgelagerter Aspekt betrachtet
wird, sondern von Anfang an integraler Bestandteil der Entwicklung, Planung und Umsetzung neuer
Offshore-Technologien ist.

## Ausbauziele Offshore-Windenergie

Die Ausbauziele für die Offshore-Windenergie im Windenergie-auf-See-Gesetz (WindSeeG) sehen vor,
dass die installierte Leistung von Offshore-Windenergieanlagen am Netz bis zum Jahr 2030 auf
insgesamt mindestens 30 GW, bis zum Jahr 2035 auf mindestens 40 GW und bis zum Jahr 2045 auf
mindestens 70 GW gesteigert wird.
Zur Erreichung der Ausbauziele, trifft das Bundes-amt für Seeschifffahrt und Hydrographie (BSH) im
Flächenentwicklungsplan (FEP) fortlaufend neue Festlegungen zum künftigen Ausbau, ins-besondere zu
den Windenergieflächen und den zugehörigen Netzanbindungen, den Kalender-jahren der Ausschreibungen
und vorgesehenen Inbetriebnahmen. Der FEP

2025 wurde im Januar 2025 veröffentlicht, im Januar 2026 folgte die erste Änderung und im Juni 2026
der Entwurf zur zweiten Änderung. Die erste Änderung legte die Verschiebung der Ausschreibungen und
Inbe-triebnahmen einiger Flächen und Netzan-bindungen fest. Der Entwurf zur zweiten Änderung sieht
weitere Verschiebungen und auch die Streichung von Ausschreibungen vor.


Insgesamt reichen die aktuellen Planungen bis 2035 und umfassen eine Gesamtleistung von ca. 41 GW.
Zur Jahresmitte verteilt sich diese auf unterschiedliche Entwicklungsstadien. Ein Anteil von 10,8 GW
befindet sich bereits in Betrieb, weitere 1,3 GW sind in Bau und für 2,6 GW wurde eine finale
Investitionsentscheidung getroffen. In der Projektrealisierung weniger weit vorange-schritten sind
17,5 GW, die einen Zuschlag bzw. Netzanbindungsanspruch vorweisen und 9 GW, die bisher lediglich für
die Ausschreibungen vor-gesehen und noch an keinen Projektentwickler vergeben sind. Damit ist das
Ausbauziel für 2030 zeitlich nicht mehr zu erreichen, das Ausbauziel für 2035 könnte bei plangemäßer
Umsetzung aller Projekte erreicht werden und für das Ausbauziel 2045 sind noch weitere Festlegungen
erforderlich.


[Grafik]

## Aktivitäten in den Offshore-Windenergieprojekten

Zur Jahresmitte 2026 befinden sich in Deutschland 31 Offshore-Windenergieprojekte (OWP) voll-ständig
in Betrieb. Im OWP Borkum Riffgrund 3 wurde die Installation der Anlagen Anfang 2025 abgeschlossen.
Im Projekt EnBW He Dreiht ist die Installation der Anlagen weitgehend abge-schlossen. In beiden
Projekten wurde bereits ein Großteil der Anlagen in Betrieb genommen, die verbleibenden Anlagen
sollen im zweiten Halbjahr 2026 folgen.

Im Nordseecluster A (NC 1 und NC 2) sowie im OWP Windanker wurden die Funda-mente zum Jahresende
2025 erfolgreich installiert. Im Nordseecluster A begann die Anlagen-installation im Juni 2026.
Diese Arbeiten wurden im OWP Windanker im Juli 2026, also im zweiten Halbjahr 2026, gestartet.
Ebenfalls im Juli 2026 war der Baubeginn im OWP Nordlicht I. Weitere 15 Projekte befinden sich noch
in einem früheren Stadium der Umsetzung.

## Wer wir sind und was wir tun

Die Stiftung wurde 2005 auf Initiative des Umweltministeriums gegründet und hat sich als
überparteiliche, überregionale und unabhängige Einrichtung zur Unterstützung der
Offshore-Windenergie etabliert.

Sie fungiert als Networking- und Kommunikationsplattform für Stakeholder aus Politik, Wirtschaft und
Wissenschaft. Ziel der Stiftung ist, die Offshore-Windenergie im Energiemix in Deutschland und
Europa zu festigen.

Die Stiftung sieht sich selbst als Think-Tank zur Entwicklung der Windenergie auf See.

## Ausbauziele Offshore-Windenergie

Die Ausbauziele für die Offshore-Windenergie im Windenergie-auf-See-Gesetz (WindSeeG) sehen vor,
dass die installierte Leistung von Offshore-Windenergieanlagen am Netz bis zum Jahr 2030 auf
insgesamt mindestens 30 GW, bis zum Jahr 2035 auf mindestens 40 GW und bis zum Jahr 2045 auf
mindestens 70 GW gesteigert wird.
Zur Erreichung der Ausbauziele, trifft das Bundes-amt für Seeschifffahrt und Hydrographie (BSH) im
Flächenentwicklungsplan (FEP) fortlaufend neue Festlegungen zum künftigen Ausbau, ins-besondere zu
den Windenergieflächen und den zugehörigen Netzanbindungen, den Kalender-jahren der Ausschreibungen
und vorgesehenen Inbetriebnahmen. Der FEP

2025 wurde im Januar 2025 veröffentlicht, im Januar 2026 folgte die erste Änderung und im Juni 2026
der Entwurf zur zweiten Änderung. Die erste Änderung legte die Verschiebung der Ausschreibungen und
Inbe-triebnahmen einiger Flächen und Netzan-bindungen fest. Der Entwurf zur zweiten Änderung sieht
weitere Verschiebungen und auch die Streichung von Ausschreibungen vor.


Insgesamt reichen die aktuellen Planungen bis 2035 und umfassen eine Gesamtleistung von ca. 41 GW.
Zur Jahresmitte verteilt sich diese auf unterschiedliche Entwicklungsstadien. Ein Anteil von 10,8 GW
befindet sich bereits in Betrieb, weitere 1,3 GW sind in Bau und für 2,6 GW wurde eine finale
Investitionsentscheidung getroffen. In der Projektrealisierung weniger weit vorange-schritten sind
17,5 GW, die einen Zuschlag bzw. Netzanbindungsanspruch vorweisen und 9 GW, die bisher lediglich für
die Ausschreibungen vor-gesehen und noch an keinen Projektentwickler vergeben sind. Damit ist das
Ausbauziel für 2030 zeitlich nicht mehr zu erreichen, das Ausbauziel für 2035 könnte bei plangemäßer
Umsetzung aller Projekte erreicht werden und für das Ausbauziel 2045 sind noch weitere Festlegungen
erforderlich.


[Grafik]

## Aktivitäten in den Offshore-Windenergieprojekten

Zur Jahresmitte 2026 befinden sich in Deutschland 31 Offshore-Windenergieprojekte (OWP) voll-ständig
in Betrieb. Im OWP Borkum Riffgrund 3 wurde die Installation der Anlagen Anfang 2025 abgeschlossen.
Im Projekt EnBW He Dreiht ist die Installation der Anlagen weitgehend abge-schlossen. In beiden
Projekten wurde bereits ein Großteil der Anlagen in Betrieb genommen, die verbleibenden Anlagen
sollen im zweiten Halbjahr 2026 folgen.

Im Nordseecluster A (NC 1 und NC 2) sowie im OWP Windanker wurden die Funda-mente zum Jahresende
2025 erfolgreich installiert. Im Nordseecluster A begann die Anlagen-installation im Juni 2026.
Diese Arbeiten wurden im OWP Windanker im Juli 2026, also im zweiten Halbjahr 2026, gestartet.
Ebenfalls im Juli 2026 war der Baubeginn im OWP Nordlicht I. Weitere 15 Projekte befinden sich noch
in einem früheren Stadium der Umsetzung.

## Wer wir sind und was wir tun

Die Stiftung wurde 2005 auf Initiative des Umweltministeriums gegründet und hat sich als
überparteiliche, überregionale und unabhängige Einrichtung zur Unterstützung der
Offshore-Windenergie etabliert.

Sie fungiert als Networking- und Kommunikationsplattform für Stakeholder aus Politik, Wirtschaft und
Wissenschaft. Ziel der Stiftung ist, die Offshore-Windenergie im Energiemix in Deutschland und
Europa zu festigen.

Die Stiftung sieht sich selbst als Think-Tank zur Entwicklung der Windenergie auf See.

# About Offshore-Windindustry.com

Offshore wind energy is developing into a new, dynamic, growing industry sector mainly in Europe and
in Asia. Businesses from the maritime economy and the wind energy sector are coming together into a
new industry sector. The website www.offshore-windindustry.com is a showcase for companies and
stakeholders from the offshore wind energy and their offerings, products and services. In addition
to industry stakeholders, a branch of research into offshore wind energy has developed with the
establishment of offshore research facilities for this future-oriented sector around the world.
Universities and educational institutions are offering new or expanded options for education and
training in the domain of offshore wind energy exploitation.

An additional focus of the website is to highlight the development of offshore wind energy and
particularly the expansion of wind energy in different countries. The development of offshore wind
farms in Europe, in parallel with the [decline in North Sea oil][50], is resulting in increased
“green“ electricity production from the sea. The offshore calendar of events gives details of
important trade fairs, events, seminars and conferences relating to wind energy. The jobs portal is
aimed at advertising new job opportunities in the offshore wind energy sector.

  #### [ Adwen GmbH ][62]
  
  Adwen is a 50/50 joint venture between AREVA and GAMESA, two global energy leaders.With a 2.8-GW
  pipeline, 5 MW and 8 MW turbines, and extensive capabilities in offshore wind, Adwen aims to
  achieve a 20% market share in Europe by 2020. The joint-venture is responsible for the design,
  manufacturing, installation, commissioning and services of offshore wind turbines. [Read More][63]
* [image]
  
  #### [ PNE Wind AG ][64]
  
  With its headquarters in Cuxhaven, the PNE WIND Group plans and realises wind farm projects on
  land and on the high seas. In doing so, its core competence lies in the development, planning,
  financing, operation, sales and service of wind farms. To date, the PNE Wind Group has already
  developed wind farms with a total nominal output amounting to more than 2,000 MW. [Read More][65]
* [image]
  
  #### [ wpd AG ][66]
  
  wpd is a developer and operator of wind farms both onshore and offshore, acting worldwide. Over
  the last 20 years, wpd has installed 1,900 wind turbines with a total of 3,600 MW. Currently 1,200
  MW are held as assets. A group staff of 1,500 is committed to wind energy in 18 countries.
  Internationally, wpd is planning projects in the scope of 6,700 MW onshore and 8,000 MW offshore.

# About Offshore-Windindustry.com

Offshore wind energy is developing into a new, dynamic, growing industry sector mainly in Europe and
in Asia. Businesses from the maritime economy and the wind energy sector are coming together into a
new industry sector. The website www.offshore-windindustry.com is a showcase for companies and
stakeholders from the offshore wind energy and their offerings, products and services. In addition
to industry stakeholders, a branch of research into offshore wind energy has developed with the
establishment of offshore research facilities for this future-oriented sector around the world.
Universities and educational institutions are offering new or expanded options for education and
training in the domain of offshore wind energy exploitation.

An additional focus of the website is to highlight the development of offshore wind energy and
particularly the expansion of wind energy in different countries. The development of offshore wind
farms in Europe, in parallel with the [decline in North Sea oil][50], is resulting in increased
“green“ electricity production from the sea. The offshore calendar of events gives details of
important trade fairs, events, seminars and conferences relating to wind energy. The jobs portal is
aimed at advertising new job opportunities in the offshore wind energy sector.

  #### [ Adwen GmbH ][62]
  
  Adwen is a 50/50 joint venture between AREVA and GAMESA, two global energy leaders.With a 2.8-GW
  pipeline, 5 MW and 8 MW turbines, and extensive capabilities in offshore wind, Adwen aims to
  achieve a 20% market share in Europe by 2020. The joint-venture is responsible for the design,
  manufacturing, installation, commissioning and services of offshore wind turbines. [Read More][63]
* [image]
  
  #### [ PNE Wind AG ][64]
  
  With its headquarters in Cuxhaven, the PNE WIND Group plans and realises wind farm projects on
  land and on the high seas. In doing so, its core competence lies in the development, planning,
  financing, operation, sales and service of wind farms. To date, the PNE Wind Group has already
  developed wind farms with a total nominal output amounting to more than 2,000 MW. [Read More][65]
* [image]
  
  #### [ wpd AG ][66]
  
  wpd is a developer and operator of wind farms both onshore and offshore, acting worldwide. Over
  the last 20 years, wpd has installed 1,900 wind turbines with a total of 3,600 MW. Currently 1,200
  MW are held as assets. A group staff of 1,500 is committed to wind energy in 18 countries.
  Internationally, wpd is planning projects in the scope of 6,700 MW onshore and 8,000 MW offshore.

APPROACHING THE FUTURE

Empowering the Future with Wind

Wind Energy Solutions

Offshore Wind Power Consulting, based in Palma de Mallorca, Spain, is a highly experienced company
in the wind energy sector. They offer guidance and effective management practices, drawing from a
skilled team and a wealth of industry knowledge. Their active involvement in offshore wind farm
management, construction, and maintenance sets them apart as a trusted partner in the field.

About us

Offshore Wind Power Consulting is a dynamic company with years of experience in the wind energy
sector. Based in Palma de Mallorca, Spain, we provide expert guidance and management, ensuring
informed operational and business decisions. As part of an experienced industry group, we leverage
extensive resources and insights to enhance the quality and range of services for our clients.

OUR STRENGTH

Project Development

Including the Project Execution Plan, preparation of ITTs, contract strategies and planning of the
design, fabrication and construction stages.

Tender and contract negotiation

Evaluation of tenders and contract negotiation, including main contractors, subcontractors, vessels,
etc.

Windfarm construction

Supply of Key resources in the organisation structure, set up of interfaces between contractors,
creation of procedures and processes.

Commissioning & Testing

Training of offshore teams, creation of procedures, vessel manifests, work orders, etc. Marine
coordination services including permit to work management.

Operations And Maintenance

Practical support to meet the requirements of the operations and maintenance regime for an offshore
wind farm. This includes vessel sourcing, QHSE Management, Site management, offshore supervision and
component exchange.

Global Wind Energy Expertise

O.S. Energy

# Enabling Offshore Wind to Push Our World Forward.

O.S. Energy supports your offshore project with specialised multi-purpose offshore vessels, a wide
range of services, and a dedicated back office team. Our customized solutions combine
state-of-the-art technology, top-level expertise, and over 20 years of experience.
[Our Services][9][Meet our fleet][10]

Who we work for

## Turning Offshore Challenges Into Reliable Solutions.

O.S. Energy is a trusted and experienced shipping partner for offshore wind park owners, operators,
private and public enterprises, as well as researchers and institutions.

[Find out more][11]

What we do

## We Get the
## Job Done.

O.S. Energy provides specially equipped vessels for all tasks around your offshore project. This
includes state-of-the-art equipment and installations of all sizes. We are your reliable partner
from start to finish – and beyond. Offshore, but never offline.
[Discover our services][12]
[Crew performing maintenance on O.S. Energy service vessel deck in North Sea]

### Let’s Keep the Future Afloat. Together.

Offshore to the core: At O.S. Energy, we work hard to provide the ideal support for your project. No

# The Renewable Energy Consultants

The Renewable Energy Consultants.

OWC combines a legacy in offshore wind, multi-disciplinary engineering expertise and market
experience across renewable energies offshore and onshore, to support the commercial development of
wind power, solar PV, hydrogen and energy storage solutions with the most comprehensive technical
offering in engineering, consultancy and advisory.

## Dedicated renewable energy consultants, from concept to operations

OWC has worked with clients on wind power projects since 2011, but as a multi-disciplinary renewable
energy consultancy, we’re equipped to deliver results across a wide range of sectors. If there is an
emerging renewable energy market, we’ll be there to help you develop a strategy and achieve
consistent results.

**Discover our experience across the sectors**

we’ll support you every step of the way.

Solar-powered renewables are the fastest-growing renewable technology. With over 20 experts around
the world, we can help you to succeed in this high-demand sector.
[Find out more ][69]

Through our sister company INNOSEA, OWC will work with you on technical, advisory, engineering and
marine assurance services to support the development of ocean energy technologies.
[Find out more ][75]

### [Floating Solar][77]

Floating photovoltaic (FPV) technology is still in its infancy, so our dedicated renewable energy
consultants can work with you to provide market-leading support for your project.
[Find out more ][78]

life-cycle projects across production, storage, and transportation.

## [Beyond roads: Inland shipping is China’s next electrification frontier][72]

July 24, 2026

By the end of 2024, China had more than 440 electric ships in operation, with ferries accounting for
97% of the total fleet. This is not surprising given the relatively high technical and
economic feasibility of electrifying small ferries operating on short, fixed routes. Yet the real
story lies beyond ferries: China has begun electrifying cargo ships—traditionally considered far
more difficult to electrify due to their larger energy demand and more complex operational
requirements—primarily for use along inland waterways. Electrifying China’s inland shipping industry
at scale will require overcoming multiple barriers, including financial and operational constraints
to the adoption of electric cargo ships. But well-designed, coordinated policy can chart the course
forward.

## [A plan to make Europe the first electro-continent][77]

July 24, 2026

The Commission has unveiled a new electrification action plan aimed at speeding up the shift from
fossil fuels to electricity in Europe across industry, transport and buildings. The goal is to make
Europe the world's first "electro-powered" continent by aiming to increase electrification from
today's 23% of energy use to 46% by 2040. By reaching this goal, the EU could save €260 billion per
year in fossil fuel imports. The new plan proposes a series of measures that will help reduce the
price gap between electricity and fossil energy costs and by incentivising the uptake of cleaner,
electricity-based technologies such as heat pumps, electric vehicles and batteries, among others.

## [Digital Upgrade: Growing role of automation in enhancing renewable power operations][82]

July 20, 2026

With renewable energy capacity expanding rapidly, power plants are increasingly using automation and
digital tools to handle more complex operations and improve efficiency. Automation in the sector has
progressed steadily, moving from basic mechanisation to advanced systems such as programmable logic
controllers and supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) platforms. At present, technologies
such as artificial intelligence (AI), drones, robotics and internet of things (IoT) are enabling
real-time monitoring, predictive maintenance and better forecasting of power generation. Automated
systems also allow operators to centrally monitor and remotely manage renewable assets across
multiple locations, helping reduce downtime, lower losses and improve overall plant performance.

## [Building Malaysia’s Clean Power System: Report][93]

July 22, 2026

Malaysia has established strong foundations for an orderly and gradual transition away from coal
power, underpinned by a commitment not to build new coal power generation and a final transition
date of 2044. Its policy and regulatory framework, along with its long-term goal to reach a 70%
share of renewables by 2050, provide a strong basis for the country to capitalize on its natural
assets and develop cheaper and more sustainable electricity generation alternatives. This transition
offers profound benefits for Malaysians, including lower-cost renewable energy, less pollution and
reduced exposure to fuel import costs and volatility. However, it is not without challenges. A
renewables led system will need to be stabilized with additional baseload or “firm” power as coal
gradually exits.

July 24, 2026

97% of the total fleet. This is not surprising given the relatively high technical and
economic feasibility of electrifying small ferries operating on short, fixed routes. Yet the real
story lies beyond ferries: China has begun electrifying cargo ships—traditionally considered far
more difficult to electrify due to their larger energy demand and more complex operational
requirements—primarily for use along inland waterways. Electrifying China’s inland shipping industry
at scale will require overcoming multiple barriers, including financial and operational constraints

today's 23% of energy use to 46% by 2040. By reaching this goal, the EU could save €260 billion per

price gap between electricity and fossil energy costs and by incentivising the uptake of cleaner,

* [Cable Laying Services][75]
  Cable Laying Services
  
  **Seaway7 offers submarine cable- and subsea umbilical installation, repair and maintenance
  services.**
  
  Related services such as dive and Remote Operated Vehicle (ROV) support, marine survey, Unexploded
  Ordnance (UXO) investigation and remedial cable protection services are also provided.
  
  [Read More][76]
* [WTG Foundations][77]
  WTG Foundations
  
  **Seaway7 offers installation services for WTG foundations utilising their ground-breaking custom
  built foundation installation vessel Seaway Alfa Lift as well as their established Heavy Lift
  Vessels (HLV), *Seaway Strashnov* and *Seaway Alfa Lift*.**
  
  In the last 12 years Seaway7 has built up an extensive track record in installing a wide range of
  foundation types, ranging from monopiles and suction bucket jackets to tripod and pre-piled
  jackets using a pile installation frame.
  
  [Read More][78]
* [Offshore Substations][79]
  Offshore Substations
  
  **Using our Heavy Lift Vessels, Seaway7 can provide the transportation and installation of
  offshore substation jackets and topsides. Mid 2020, we had successfully installed more than 30
  HVAC platforms.**
  
  The DP3 HLV *Seaway Strashnov* with its 5000t crane is especially well equipped for this work.
  
  [Read More][80]
* [Wind Turbines][81]
  Wind Turbines
  
  **Seaway7 provides fully integrated Transport and Installation (T&I) services for offshore wind
  turbine generators (WTGs) utilising the company’s next generation jack-up installation vessel
  *Seaway Ventus*.**
  
  With the organisation, people, vessels and systems in place, and a strong track record – Seaway7
  are the ideal partner for the installation of offshore windfarms.
  
  [Read More][82]
* [Heavy Transportation][83]
  Heavy Transportation
  
  **Seaway7 is one of the most experienced heavy transport vessel operators in the world, providing
  highly engineered transportation solutions for the most demanding cargoes – safely and on time.**
  
  The six Seaway7 open deck semi-submersible heavy transportation vessels; Eagle, Falcon, Hawk,
  Osprey, Swan and Albatross are suitable for dry transportation of offshore wind foundations,
  offshore modules and all other oversized floating and non-floating cargoes.
  
  [Read More][84]

built an industry-leading track record in installing WTG foundations, substations and inner array
cables for many of the key offshore wind developers in Europe, Taiwan and the US.**

## Our services

Our offshore experience in the energy sector spans three decades, successfully completing over 50
[projects][85] and transferring offshore knowledge gained in the oil and gas industry to support the
energy transition and offshore fixed wind market.

Seaway7 has been active in the offshore Renewables Energy industry since 2009, when we installed our
first Wind Turbine Generator (WTG) monopile foundation offshore in the UK, and has since built an
industry-leading track record in installing WTG foundations, substations and inner array cables for
many of the key offshore wind developers in Europe, Taiwan and the US.

To date Seaway7 has installed over 800 wind turbine generator foundations, 30 substations and 2500km
of inner array cables.

* [Cable Laying Services][75]
  Cable Laying Services
  
  **Seaway7 offers submarine cable- and subsea umbilical installation, repair and maintenance
  services.**
  
  Related services such as dive and Remote Operated Vehicle (ROV) support, marine survey, Unexploded
  Ordnance (UXO) investigation and remedial cable protection services are also provided.
  
  [Read More][76]
* [WTG Foundations][77]
  WTG Foundations
  
  **Seaway7 offers installation services for WTG foundations utilising their ground-breaking custom
  built foundation installation vessel Seaway Alfa Lift as well as their established Heavy Lift
  Vessels (HLV), *Seaway Strashnov* and *Seaway Alfa Lift*.**
  
  In the last 12 years Seaway7 has built up an extensive track record in installing a wide range of
  foundation types, ranging from monopiles and suction bucket jackets to tripod and pre-piled
  jackets using a pile installation frame.
  
  [Read More][78]
* [Offshore Substations][79]
  Offshore Substations
  
  **Using our Heavy Lift Vessels, Seaway7 can provide the transportation and installation of
  offshore substation jackets and topsides. Mid 2020, we had successfully installed more than 30
  HVAC platforms.**
  
  The DP3 HLV *Seaway Strashnov* with its 5000t crane is especially well equipped for this work.
  
  [Read More][80]
* [Wind Turbines][81]
  Wind Turbines
  
  **Seaway7 provides fully integrated Transport and Installation (T&I) services for offshore wind
  turbine generators (WTGs) utilising the company’s next generation jack-up installation vessel
  *Seaway Ventus*.**
  
  With the organisation, people, vessels and systems in place, and a strong track record – Seaway7
  are the ideal partner for the installation of offshore windfarms.
  
  [Read More][82]
* [Heavy Transportation][83]
  Heavy Transportation
  
  **Seaway7 is one of the most experienced heavy transport vessel operators in the world, providing
  highly engineered transportation solutions for the most demanding cargoes – safely and on time.**
  
  The six Seaway7 open deck semi-submersible heavy transportation vessels; Eagle, Falcon, Hawk,
  Osprey, Swan and Albatross are suitable for dry transportation of offshore wind foundations,
  offshore modules and all other oversized floating and non-floating cargoes.
  
  [Read More][84]

cables for many of the key offshore wind developers in Europe, Taiwan and the US.**

## Our services

Our offshore experience in the energy sector spans three decades, successfully completing over 50
[projects][85] and transferring offshore knowledge gained in the oil and gas industry to support the
energy transition and offshore fixed wind market.

Seaway7 has been active in the offshore Renewables Energy industry since 2009, when we installed our
first Wind Turbine Generator (WTG) monopile foundation offshore in the UK, and has since built an
industry-leading track record in installing WTG foundations, substations and inner array cables for
many of the key offshore wind developers in Europe, Taiwan and the US.

To date Seaway7 has installed over 800 wind turbine generator foundations, 30 substations and 2500km
of inner array cables.

## sustainable energy solutions

Wind Systems LTD (SG)** revolves around the development and deployment of sustainable energy

installing, developing, and servicing wind energy and hybrid projects all over the world. Our

crucial role in laying the foundations for the sustainable era, and that we are uniquely positioned
to show the path to a sustainable planet.

Wind energy is our heritage and core competence. We believe wind will form the backbone of the
sustainable energy systems of the future, and we remain focused on developing solutions that
accelerate the energy transition and strengthen SG’s continued leadership in wind.

# Real knowledge about offshore energy

Anywhere in the world, we find the right people for the right job in offshore energy. No task is
beyond our limits and no question is too small. We are there for you.

[Man my project][19]
[Find a job][20]

#### Construction & Service Personnel

Our team consists of experts with hands-on experience in offshore operations such as pipelay,
drilling, and heavy lift operations ranging from jackets and topsides for oil & gas to substations
and wind turbines for OWF. We deliver from OCM to the rigger on deck.

#### Marine Crew

We specialise in providing top-notch marine crew exclusively for work vessels anywhere in the world,
including captains, mates, engineers, and deck crew.

#### Project Management

We offer **[project management][21]** services for new build and R&M projects of work vessels for
the oil, gas, and wind industry. We have teams of project managers, inspectors, document
controllers, contract managers, commissioning engineers, etc.

#### Operational Engineering

Whether it involves performing inclining tests, lightship weights, marine warranty inspections, or
performing operational related engineering, we have the expertise to get the job done.

#### Consultancy

We have the in-house expertise to solve your operational or technical issues, to advise or to
support tender processes or market research.

#### Staff & Backoffice

We deliver recruitment solutions tailored to your project staffing needs. Leveraging our deep
industry expertise, we don’t just understand your requirements – we act swiftly to connect you with
the ideal candidate, ensuring your team is equipped to excel without delay.

[Our projects][22]

#### Problem solving

We solve real problems with in-depth knowledge. You will be dealing with people who understand what
your problem is and, therefore, able to a reliable solution.

#### Teamwork

We support our on-site employees with knowledge (teamwork). We invest in people and aim for a
long-term relationship.

#### Unburden

We look beyond the assignment. Our team takes care of our clients and our team members. Everything
is arranged for, from travel to important paperwork. We are always available for our crew and our
clients, anywhere, anytime!

## Solutions shaped to your business reality

**The Offshore Partners is an independent service provider to offshore wind projects, oil & gas
majors, vessel operators, offshore installation contractors, investors, project and product
developers, and public authorities worldwide. We provide technical and project management services
for new build and conversion projects, for on- and offshore installation projects, recruitment and
crewing services, as well as operational support.**

We specialise in supporting new build, conversion and R&M projects of work vessels intended for
installation projects at sea. We have the expertise to support installation work at sea and on land.
In addition, we assist with recruitment & selection of staff, and we provide crew and operational
support.

From the moment our people leave home until the moment they return, we take care of everything for
them. We are available 24 hours a day. Our aim is to enable our employees to fully concentrate on
their work at location, while we take care of everything from door to door.

### Interested in working together?

[Reach out to us][23]

## We’ve Been Building For Over 20 years

Founded in 2005, The Offshore Partners has since built a team of loyal employees, some of whom have
been with us for over a decade. Our company started with inspections and conversion projects, which
quickly led to more projects and with it a growing team of different nationalities. In 2013, we
started crewing and operational engineering.

We are both customer- and people-oriented, and put our core values of unburdening, teamwork, and

### No question is too big or too small

The Offshore Partners is an independent service provider to offshore wind projects, [ oil & gas][27]
majors, vessel operators, offshore installation contractors, investors, project and product
developers, and public authorities worldwide. We provide technical and project management services
for new build and conversion projects, for on- and offshore installation projects, recruitment & [
crewing][28], as well as operational support.
[Reach out to us][29]

##### We need a project manager in Singapore, can you arrange that?

Of course. At The Offshore Partners, we have an extensive network of qualified professionals
available worldwide. We strive to fully unburden our clients. This means that we take responsibility
for all matters that need to be arranged to get someone, anywhere in the world, to work. We ensure
that our people are trained and certified for the work they will do, we arrange visas, flights,
transport, accommodation, and, where necessary, the tax part.

##### We are stuck on a project, can we use your expertise to find a solution?

We understand how important it is to bring a project to a successful conclusion. If you get stuck on
a project, you can rely on our expertise and experience to assist you in finding a solution. Our
talented and experienced teams are up to date with the latest developments and technologies in the
offshore industry and can be part of the solution to identify and resolve the issues you encounter.

##### How do you deal with problems for which there are no standard solutions?

By using creativity, experience, and relying on out-of-the-box solutions that have arisen from
previous projects and consultation with colleagues. If we cannot solve the problem ourselves, we
always have someone in our network who can.

##### How do you deal with the shortage of technical personnel?

Through our years of experience and extensive network, we always find someone who fits our client’s
project. In addition, we can also help with recruitment for a permanent position when requested. We
have access to a large pool of project and office staff, as well as crew.

##### Do you have engineers available who can assist at the office with setting up the installation
##### method for wind farms?

Yes, at The Offshore Partners, we have a team of experienced engineers available to help you. We
understand that setting up the installation method for wind farms is a complex process and that it
is crucial to have a good plan before starting the installation. Our engineers work closely with you
to develop a plan that meets your specific requirements and takes into account all relevant factors,
such as the offshore environment, weather conditions, and available equipment and its capacities,
etc.

##### How do you deal with the growing demand for maintenance services for wind farms?

By constantly expanding and strengthening our network in order to maintain our full service level to
our clients.

### Green Octopus industry alliance

The Offshore Partners is the initiator of the Green Octopus industry alliance. The consortium,
comprises the Offshore Partners, KCI the Engineers, PricewaterhouseCoopers (PWC),Fraser Well
Management and TNO . Green Octopus is an independent collaboration that is dedicated to
decommissioning and re-use, with the appropriate capabilities right across the value chain.
[More about this project][30]

### Project case: Conversion of the ‘Amazon’ vessel

The Offshore Partners have been involved in the conversion of the ‘Amazon’, McDermott’s Deepwater
Construction Support and Pipelay Vessel, capable of executing complex infrastructure and pipeline
projects in ultra-deep water.
[More about this project][31]

**The Offshore Partners is an independent service provider to offshore wind projects, oil & gas
majors, vessel operators, offshore installation contractors, investors, project and product
developers, and public authorities worldwide. We provide technical and project management services
for new build and conversion projects, for on- and offshore installation projects, recruitment and
crewing services, as well as operational support.**

We specialise in supporting new build, conversion and R&M projects of work vessels intended for
installation projects at sea. We have the expertise to support installation work at sea and on land.
In addition, we assist with recruitment & selection of staff, and we provide crew and operational
support.

From the moment our people leave home until the moment they return, we take care of everything for
them. We are available 24 hours a day. Our aim is to enable our employees to fully concentrate on
their work at location, while we take care of everything from door to door.

### Interested in working together?

[Reach out to us][23]

## We’ve Been Building For Over 20 years

Founded in 2005, The Offshore Partners has since built a team of loyal employees, some of whom have
been with us for over a decade. Our company started with inspections and conversion projects, which
quickly led to more projects and with it a growing team of different nationalities. In 2013, we
started crewing and operational engineering.

We are both customer- and people-oriented, and put our core values of unburdening, teamwork, and
problem-solving first. We believe that our distinctiveness lies in our focus on the human side of
our work.

[HR & Project Managers][24]
[Personnel][25]
[Operational Engineering][26]

### No question is too big or too small

The Offshore Partners is an independent service provider to offshore wind projects, [ oil & gas][27]
majors, vessel operators, offshore installation contractors, investors, project and product
developers, and public authorities worldwide. We provide technical and project management services
for new build and conversion projects, for on- and offshore installation projects, recruitment & [
crewing][28], as well as operational support.
[Reach out to us][29]

##### We need a project manager in Singapore, can you arrange that?

Of course. At The Offshore Partners, we have an extensive network of qualified professionals
available worldwide. We strive to fully unburden our clients. This means that we take responsibility
for all matters that need to be arranged to get someone, anywhere in the world, to work. We ensure
that our people are trained and certified for the work they will do, we arrange visas, flights,
transport, accommodation, and, where necessary, the tax part.

##### We are stuck on a project, can we use your expertise to find a solution?

We understand how important it is to bring a project to a successful conclusion. If you get stuck on
a project, you can rely on our expertise and experience to assist you in finding a solution. Our
talented and experienced teams are up to date with the latest developments and technologies in the
offshore industry and can be part of the solution to identify and resolve the issues you encounter.

##### How do you deal with problems for which there are no standard solutions?

By using creativity, experience, and relying on out-of-the-box solutions that have arisen from
previous projects and consultation with colleagues. If we cannot solve the problem ourselves, we
always have someone in our network who can.

##### How do you deal with the shortage of technical personnel?

Through our years of experience and extensive network, we always find someone who fits our client’s
project. In addition, we can also help with recruitment for a permanent position when requested. We
have access to a large pool of project and office staff, as well as crew.

##### Do you have engineers available who can assist at the office with setting up the installation
##### method for wind farms?

Yes, at The Offshore Partners, we have a team of experienced engineers available to help you. We
understand that setting up the installation method for wind farms is a complex process and that it
is crucial to have a good plan before starting the installation. Our engineers work closely with you
to develop a plan that meets your specific requirements and takes into account all relevant factors,
such as the offshore environment, weather conditions, and available equipment and its capacities,
etc.

##### How do you deal with the growing demand for maintenance services for wind farms?

By constantly expanding and strengthening our network in order to maintain our full service level to
our clients.

### Green Octopus industry alliance

The Offshore Partners is the initiator of the Green Octopus industry alliance. The consortium,
comprises the Offshore Partners, KCI the Engineers, PricewaterhouseCoopers (PWC),Fraser Well
Management and TNO . Green Octopus is an independent collaboration that is dedicated to
decommissioning and re-use, with the appropriate capabilities right across the value chain.
[More about this project][30]

### Project case: Conversion of the ‘Amazon’ vessel

The Offshore Partners have been involved in the conversion of the ‘Amazon’, McDermott’s Deepwater
Construction Support and Pipelay Vessel, capable of executing complex infrastructure and pipeline
projects in ultra-deep water.

### [ Battery Energy Storage Systems in Viet Nam: Market Outlook, Policy Challenges and Business
### Opportunities ][87]

Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) are expected to become a cornerstone of Viet Nam's energy
transition. As renewable energy capacity expands rapidly, energy storage will play an increasingly
critical role in ensuring grid reliability, integrating variable renewable energy sources, and
supporting the country's long-term decarbonization goals. This article presents the Vietnam Energy
Association's (VEA) assessment of Viet Nam's emerging BESS market. It examines three key aspects:
market growth prospects, policy and investment challenges, and strategic opportunities for domestic
enterprises.
[View more][88]
[ [Vietnam’s Offshore Wind Target by 2030: Insights from the Government Meeting] ][89]

### [ Vietnam’s Offshore Wind Target by 2030: Insights from the Government Meeting ][90]

At a government meeting on May 19, 2026, discussing a draft Decree on special mechanisms for energy
development, Deputy Prime Ministers Pham Gia Tuc and Le Tien Chau focused significant attention on
offshore wind power, which is increasingly seen as a key pillar of Vietnam’s energy transition
strategy. Based on the meeting discussions and conclusions, Vietnam Energy Review provides several
observations and analyses.
[View more][91]
[ [Improving and perfecting the regulations for the development of gas, power projects and energy
storage systems in Vietnam for the period 2026 – 2030] ][92]

### [ Improving and perfecting the regulations for the development of gas, power projects and energy
### storage systems in Vietnam for the period 2026 – 2030 ][93]

On April 22, 2026, in Hanoi, under the chairmanship of the Electricity Authority of Vietnam
(Ministry of Industry and Trade), the Vietnam Energy Association (VEA), the Vietnam Energy Review
(VER) successfully organized the Forum on Improving and perfecting the regulations for the
development of gas, power projects and energy storage systems in Vietnam for the period 2026–2030.
The forum brought together more than 270 delegates from central and local authorities, domestic and
international businesses, and experts across the energy sector.
[View more][94]
[ [VEA Vice Chairwoman Nguyen Thi Thanh Binh elected to the 16th National Assembly] ][95]

### [ VEA Vice Chairwoman Nguyen Thi Thanh Binh elected to the 16th National Assembly ][96]

The election of deputies to the 16th National Assembly (2026–2031 tenure) has concluded
successfully. According to the Resolution announced by the National Election Council on March 21,
2026, Ms. Nguyen Thi Thanh Binh – Vice Chairwoman of the Vietnam Energy Association (VEA) – has been
elected to the 16th National Assembly.
[View more][97]
[ [Approval of the revised national energy master plan to 2030, with a vision to 2050] ][98]

### [ Approval of the revised national energy master plan to 2030, with a vision to 2050 ][99]

The Ministry of Industry and Trade has issued Decision No. 363/QD-BCT dated February 28, 2026,
approving the revised National Energy Master Plan for the 2021 - 2030 period, with a vision to 2050.
The plan covers oil and gas, coal, electricity, and new and renewable energy across the full value
chain.

### [ Battery Energy Storage Systems in Viet Nam: Market Outlook, Policy Challenges and Business
### Opportunities ][87]

Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) are expected to become a cornerstone of Viet Nam's energy
transition. As renewable energy capacity expands rapidly, energy storage will play an increasingly
critical role in ensuring grid reliability, integrating variable renewable energy sources, and
supporting the country's long-term decarbonization goals. This article presents the Vietnam Energy
Association's (VEA) assessment of Viet Nam's emerging BESS market. It examines three key aspects:
market growth prospects, policy and investment challenges, and strategic opportunities for domestic
enterprises.
[View more][88]
[ [Vietnam’s Offshore Wind Target by 2030: Insights from the Government Meeting] ][89]

### [ Vietnam’s Offshore Wind Target by 2030: Insights from the Government Meeting ][90]

At a government meeting on May 19, 2026, discussing a draft Decree on special mechanisms for energy
development, Deputy Prime Ministers Pham Gia Tuc and Le Tien Chau focused significant attention on
offshore wind power, which is increasingly seen as a key pillar of Vietnam’s energy transition
strategy. Based on the meeting discussions and conclusions, Vietnam Energy Review provides several
observations and analyses.
[View more][91]
[ [Improving and perfecting the regulations for the development of gas, power projects and energy
storage systems in Vietnam for the period 2026 – 2030] ][92]

### [ Improving and perfecting the regulations for the development of gas, power projects and energy
### storage systems in Vietnam for the period 2026 – 2030 ][93]

On April 22, 2026, in Hanoi, under the chairmanship of the Electricity Authority of Vietnam
(Ministry of Industry and Trade), the Vietnam Energy Association (VEA), the Vietnam Energy Review
(VER) successfully organized the Forum on Improving and perfecting the regulations for the
development of gas, power projects and energy storage systems in Vietnam for the period 2026–2030.
The forum brought together more than 270 delegates from central and local authorities, domestic and
international businesses, and experts across the energy sector.
[View more][94]

### [ VEA Vice Chairwoman Nguyen Thi Thanh Binh elected to the 16th National Assembly ][96]

The election of deputies to the 16th National Assembly (2026–2031 tenure) has concluded
successfully. According to the Resolution announced by the National Election Council on March 21,
2026, Ms. Nguyen Thi Thanh Binh – Vice Chairwoman of the Vietnam Energy Association (VEA) – has been
elected to the 16th National Assembly.
[View more][97]
[ [Approval of the revised national energy master plan to 2030, with a vision to 2050] ][98]

### [ Approval of the revised national energy master plan to 2030, with a vision to 2050 ][99]

The Ministry of Industry and Trade has issued Decision No. 363/QD-BCT dated February 28, 2026,
approving the revised National Energy Master Plan for the 2021 - 2030 period, with a vision to 2050.
The plan covers oil and gas, coal, electricity, and new and renewable energy across the full value
chain.

# Your global full scope **maritime**** safety partner**

What if you only had to rely on one proven partner for all your maritime safety needs?

**VIKING Life-Saving Equipment** brings you all the solutions you need to stay safe and
compliant. Our range includes everything from lifeboats, fast rescue boats and evacuation systems to
liferafts, personal protective gear, firefighting equipment and safety training.

Powered by the industry’s strongest network, we provide worldwide multi-brand equipment service with
OEM quality and support the thousands of maritime and offshore operators who prefer subscribing to
safety compliance with a fixed price safety agreement.

# Shaping the decarbonisation of marine and energy


Our everyday lives depend on a steady supply of electricity and goods shipped to us from across the
world.

Yet, marine and energy generate over a third of global greenhouse gases. That’s why we’re shaping
the decarbonisation of marine and energy.

[About us][8]

for shipping and energy

## Enabling you to cut emissions at sea and on land

We help our customers take a decarbonisation journey that is environmentally sustainable and
financially viable.

[Senayan power plant in Indonesia]
[lightning-icon]
Energy

We help the energy sector accelerate the transition towards a 100% renewable energy future with our
market-leading technologies and power system expertise. Energy providers globally rely on our
flexible engine power plants, energy storage systems, intelligent optimisation technologies, and
lifecycle services. With reliable, affordable, and sustainable power as your goal, our solutions
support you in ramping up and balancing intermittent renewables.

[Wärtsilä in energy][9]
[Gas tanker on open sea]
[marine-icon]
Marine

With Wärtsilä as your partner, your maritime operations can be smarter, cleaner, and more efficient.
One in three of the world’s large vessels already relies on our technologies – power, propulsion and
other solutions – because you value reliability, safety, and performance. And as the industry moves
toward alternative fuels and digital ecosystems, we help you stay ahead with our future-proof
solutions.

[Wärtsilä in marine][10]
[Power plant in the desert]
[Service men at pier]
[Freight vessel in port]

## Interim report for April-June 2026 has been published

In the second quarter of 2026, Wärtsilä’s total order intake increased by 33% to 2,849 MEUR to an
all-time high quarter, contributing to an all-time high order book of 8,976 MEUR. The operating
result increased by 14% to EUR 209 million, representing 13.4% of net sales. Cash flow from
operating activities increased to EUR 497 million.

[Read more][11]

## Global impact. Succeeding together.

From world-first technology launches to performance-based agreements, we innovate to create value
with our customers and partners.

[
Solvang

Onboard carbon capture successfully cuts CO2 emissions by 70% for Solvang’s Clipper Eris carrier

][12][
Aqualectra, Curacao

Installed a new 38.4 MW grid balancing engine power plant in addition to the 25 MW / 45 MWh Energy
Storage System installed earlier.

][13][
GIGA Storage BV

Installed Wärtsilä's 25 MW / 48 MWh energy storage in the Netherlands, improving grid stability and
scaling renewable integration.

][14][
Viking Line

Finnish ferry company Viking Line is a market leader in passenger transport in the northern Baltic
Sea region.

][15][
United Power

United Power manages over 2,137 MW of installed capacity in Bangladesh, of which 1,066 MW is powered
by Wärtsilä engines.

][16][
Clearway Energy

Partnered with Wärtsilä for storage solutions supporting reliable renewable energy in California and
Hawaii.

][17]
[leaf-icon]
Green is not black or white.

While no single solution will carry us through the transition, we already have most of the
technology needed to decarbonise. From engines that run flexibly on low- and zero-carbon fuels to
AI-driven predictive analytics, we are using all tools in the toolbox to help our customers take the
next step on their decarbonisation journey.

Impalex GmbH

Benjamin Oppermann
Windpark Kahler Kopf GmbH & Co. KG

### Why wind asset owners are turning their attention to optimisation

As Andreas Berg Nielsen steps into the role of CEO at Windar Photonics, he believes the wind
industry is entering a new phase, one focused less on building bigger turbines and more on
extracting greater performance from existing assets. In this interview, he explains why optimisation
is becoming a core priority for asset owners, how Windar’s LiDAR technology is delivering measurable
returns within months and why the company sees enormous growth potential in the world’s ageing wind
fleet.

onshore build-out across Scotland and Wales to the rise of giants such as Dogger Bank, Hornsea and
Seagreen in the North Sea, wind has moved from challenger technology to the largest single source of
UK electricity.
